newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Dull except for two players.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Dull except for two players.

text.p: Most traders took a half day off on Thursday before the long weekend holiday in Singapore with the exception of the two players who had dominated the market the whole week, traders said.

A Dutch trader emerged already in the morning offering 97-octane lifting early March at $28.05 per barrel fob Singapore, and bidding for 92-octane lifting February 21-25 at $26.90, both 5 cents higher than his levels on Wednesday.
The offer for 95-octane did not reappear after having being sold Wednesday to a U.S. major at $27.10 per barrel fob Singapore.
"It is not a bad price considering the spread to 92-octane," a trader said.
He said the spread was normally up to $1.00 per barrel but based on the talking levels, it was traded only 30 cents higher than the lower octane material.
Naphtha February swaps firmed to $24.50/$24.90 per barrel, up from Wednesday's late bid at $24.30.
